observation_summary: The compiler incorrectly fails to resolve prototype methods when a constructor's prototype is explicitly defined using an object literal, leading to 'Property never defined' warnings.
hypothesis: The compiler's type inference logic for prototype inheritance is flawed when an object literal is assigned to a prototype. It fails to correctly link the implicit prototype of the object literal to the superclass's prototype, causing the compiler to lose track of inherited properties.
prediction: The fix will involve updating the type inference logic to explicitly reset or link the implicit prototype of the object literal assigned to the constructor's prototype, ensuring that inherited properties are correctly resolved.
experiment_rationale: The fix diff shows that in TypedScopeCreator, the compiler now explicitly calls `typeRegistry.resetImplicitPrototype` when an object literal is assigned to a prototype, and in FunctionType, it manages the association of the prototype more carefully. This confirms the issue was an incorrect algorithmic handling of prototype chains during type inference.
reasoning_summary: The bug is caused by an incorrect implementation of the prototype inheritance resolution algorithm during type inference. The fix involves modifying the logic that handles prototype assignments (specifically for object literals) to correctly maintain the prototype chain. This is a procedural/algorithmic correction in how the compiler computes type relationships, fitting the 'Algorithm/Method' category.
evidence_used: The fix diff in TypedScopeCreator adds logic to reset the implicit prototype of an object literal.
The fix diff in FunctionType adds logic to manage the association of the old prototype.
The failing tests indicate that the compiler fails to recognize properties defined on the prototype when using specific inheritance patterns.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While the fix involves maintaining a relationship between prototypes, the root cause is the procedural logic (algorithm) used by the compiler to infer these relationships during type checking.
